_doc: #1832 MARKZ (formerly MY-PM): the owner's page 'Portfolio Returns After Inflation & Taxes (EUR MoM)' (Portfolio_Returns_Sensitivity_Matrix.html, PortfolioLab) drawn natively by ui/MarkzPage.kt from this declaration; Markz.kt holds the arithmetic (pure), MarkzStats.kt the statistics of the Markovitz substeps. Every tab, input, output, table, chart and word of the owner's page is here: `tabs` (the page's top row; each is a MARKZ sub-page, build.json ui.stacks.markz `view`), `defaults` (the page's DEFAULTS), `inputs` (the 14 parameters of the two-column table and the 3 Steps, by the page's element ids), `words`, `heat` (the diverging heatmap of the matrix), `frontier` (the Markovitz page's frontier portfolios and its efficient-frontier diagram, in the page's 420 x 220 SVG units), `methodology` (its five steps) and `substeps` (Volatility, Beta, CAPM Calculator, Correlation, Optimization: the page's texts and links). The owner's page left the five substeps as descriptions; MARKZ implements them (`stats`): the daily closes of the declared instruments from the app's quote source (data/quotes.json), the estimators and the optimiser named in `stats`, nothing typed as a market figure. Rule 16: MarkzParityTest holds every element; Rename1832ParityTest holds every MY-PM element under MARKZ.

words.mk_title: How a Markovitz Analysis Is Done
words.mk_intro: Developed by Harry Markowitz (1952), a Mean-Variance Optimization evaluates assets not in isolation, but by how their expected returns, volatilities, and correlations interact—identifying the Efficient Frontier of portfolios that maximize return for any given level of risk.

methodology.title: Estimate Return & Risk
methodology.text: Define the investable assets (e.g., sovereign bonds, equities, cash) and estimate each asset's expected annual return (μᵢ) and standard deviation / volatility (σᵢ).

methodology.title: Covariance Matrix
methodology.text: Measure pairwise correlations (ρᵢⱼ) between every pair of assets. Combining assets with ρ < 1 cancels out idiosyncratic swings—the mathematical engine of diversification.

methodology.title: Portfolio Math
methodology.text: For any weight mix w (∑wᵢ = 1): E(Rp) = ∑ wᵢμᵢ ; σp = √(∑∑ wᵢwⱼρᵢⱼσᵢσⱼ)

methodology.title: Efficient Frontier
methodology.text: Run quadratic optimization across return targets to find the minimum-variance weights for each return level. Plotting (σp, E(Rp)) forms the upper boundary known as the Efficient Frontier.

methodology.title: Optimal Selection
methodology.text: Select either the Max Sharpe (Tangency) portfolio for highest risk-adjusted efficiency, or the frontier portfolio matching your required Sensy Matrix monthly income.

substeps.title: Volatility
substeps.text: Studies and compares candidate volatility estimators (Historical Standard Deviation, EWMA, GARCH, and Implied Volatility) to decide which measure best captures asset and market risk before calculating Beta and the covariance matrix.

substeps.title: Beta
substeps.text: Measures each asset's systematic sensitivity (βᵢ = Cov(Rᵢ, Rₘ) / σₘ²) using our selected volatility framework to quantify how strongly individual holdings amplify or dampen broader benchmark movements.

substeps.title: CAPM Calculator
substeps.text: Serves as our benchmark expected-return calculator (E(Rᵢ) = Rᶠ + βᵢ (E(Rₘ) − Rᶠ)), combining the risk-free rate, asset Beta, and market risk premium to establish the baseline return input for portfolio optimization.

substeps.title: Correlation
substeps.text: Evaluates pairwise return correlations (ρᵢⱼ) and builds the variance-covariance matrix (Σ) across asset classes and currencies to determine how effectively low-correlated holdings reduce overall portfolio variance.

substeps.title: Optimization
substeps.text: Solves for optimal asset weights (w) along the Efficient Frontier and maximizes the Sharpe Ratio ((Rₚ − Rᶠ) / σₚ) to output the target portfolio return for the Sensy Matrix.

stats._doc: The substeps' data: the daily closes of `assets` and `benchmark` (and `implied` for the implied volatility) from the quote source of data/quotes.json (range 5y, daily); simple daily returns on the days every series has, the last `window_days`; volatilities annualised by sqrt(annual_days). Historical SD = the sample standard deviation; EWMA = RiskMetrics with lambda `ewma_lambda`; GARCH(1,1) = variance targeting (omega = (1 - alpha - beta) x the sample variance) with the declared alpha and beta, run through the window, its last conditional variance; Implied = the declared volatility index's last close (an asset without one is n/a). Beta = rho(i, m) x sigma_i / sigma_m with the selected framework's sigmas; CAPM E(Ri) = Rf + beta_i (E(Rm) - Rf); Sigma_ij = rho_ij sigma_i sigma_j; the optimiser searches the long-only weights on a `grid_step` grid (sum 1) for the minimum variance, the maximum Sharpe ((E(Rp) - Rf) / sigma_p) and the minimum variance at each return of the frontier.
